report.title: Red Lions edge Blue Sharks in extra-time chaos
report.summary: Red Lions beat Blue Sharks 3-2 after extra time. Fox scored first in the 28th minute for Red Lions, Gray levelled in the 62nd, Reid put Red Lions back ahead in the 95th, Cruz made it 2-2 in the 105th, and Bell of Blue Sharks put the decisive own goal into Blue Sharks’ net in the 113th. The match stayed open right to the end, with the late extra-time spell producing the final two goals.

sections.text: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth right to the end. Fox put Red Lions ahead at 28', Gray levelled for Blue Sharks at 62', and Reid restored the lead at 95' before Cruz made it 2-2 at 105'. The last twist came at 113', when Bell of Blue Sharks put the ball into Blue Sharks' own net, and that counted for Red Lions.

Red Lions controlled the match overall, with 69% possession, 85% of final-third actions, and a far higher average line than Blue Sharks. Red Lions also moved the ball far more often and far higher up the pitch, finishing with 838 passes, 93% accuracy, and 110 entries into the final third, compared with Blue Sharks' 376 passes, 85% accuracy, and 31 final-third entries. Red Lions also led the shot metrics, with 27 shots, 11 on target and 6 big chances to Blue Sharks' 15 shots, 7 on target and 5 big chances.

Red Lions controlled the game for most of the night and finished with 69% possession, 85% of the territory and 110 entries into the final third. Blue Sharks stayed in it through moments of pressure and managed 5 big chances from fewer attacks, but Red Lions created more throughout with 27 shots, 11 on target and 6 big chances to Blue Sharks' 15 shots, 7 on target and 5 big chances.

The turning point was the spell between 95' and 113': Reid's extra-time goal got Red Lions back in front, then the own goal flipped the match for good. Lane, Rook and Fox all had a hand in the Red Lions story, with Reid's strike and the late break from Bell's own net proving enough to send the home side away with the win.

analyst.title: Red Lions Edge a Wild Extra-Time Battle
paragraphs: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth before ending in chaos. Fox gave Red Lions the lead in the 28th minute, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, and Reid restored Red Lions' advantage in the 95th. Cruz pulled Blue Sharks back level in the 105th, before Bell of Blue Sharks put the ball into Blue Sharks' own net in the 113th, which counted for Red Lions.

Red Lions controlled the match overall, with 69% possession, 85% of final-third actions, and a far higher average line than Blue Sharks. Red Lions also moved the ball far more often and far higher up the pitch, finishing with 838 passes, 93% accuracy, and 110 entries into the final third, compared with Blue Sharks' 376 passes, 85% accuracy, and 31 final-third entries.

The turning point was Red Lions' ability to keep coming forward in extra time, with Reid's 95th-minute goal and the own goal from Bell ending Blue Sharks' hopes of taking control. The last 10 minutes were chaotic, but Red Lions spent almost all of that spell in Blue Sharks' half and held the match there until the final whistle.
